subject: Trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

messages.author: d3700dd3210d01b2
messages.subject: Trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix
parts:
Hi lavaan group,

I am fitting a CFA with latent variables that capture different cognitive domains (memory, language, visuospatial ability, executive function, and orientation). Orientation is measured as a latent variable capturing the correlation between two lower order latent variables measuring orientation to time and orientation to space. This model uses a mixture of continuous and categorical indicators and is estimated using the WLSMV estimator.

However, the model gives me an error message that I had not seen before: 

"In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix"

I have seen related error messages posted in the Google Group, but this does not seem to have been solved in prior posts. For reference, I am posting the model syntax as well as the fitting statement below. Any assistance in addressing this warning message would be greatly appreciated.

cog5fc <- '
# latent variables
mem =~ mem1 + mem2 + mem3 + mem4 + mem5 + mem6 + mem7
lan =~ lan1 + lan2 + lan3 + lan4 + lan5 + lan6 + lan7 + lan8
vis =~ vis1 + vis2 + vis3
exfx =~  exfx1 + exfx2 + exfx3 + exfx4 + exfx5
orient1 =~ time1 + time2 + time3 + time4 + time5
orient2 =~ place1 + place2 + place3
orient =~ a*orient1 + a*orient2

# covariance of latent variables
orient~~lan + vis + exfx + mem
mem~~lan + vis + exfx
lan~~vis + exfx
vis~~exfx

'

cog5fc.fit <- sem(cog5fc, data=mi, estimator="WLSMV", missing="pairwise", ordered=c("lan2", "lan3", "lan4", "lan5", "lan6", "lan7", "lan8", "vis1", "time1", "time2", "time3", "time4", "time5", "place1", "place2", "place3"), std.lv=TRUE, parameterization="delta")

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: Trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix
parts:
When you construct a matrix with pairwise methods, it is not guaranteed to be positive definite (see Wothke's chapter in Bollen and Long (1993) Testing SEMs book https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/testing-structural-equation-models/book3893#contents; Wothke was a lead developer of AMOS, so he had seen a fair share of linear algebra problems in his product). Generalized inverse is the best you can do. It's a warning, it's not an error. If you can do anything... get better data :).
